---
title: "EdgeR DEG analysis using FeatureCounts output"
output: html_notebook
---

Notes: This is a work in progress R script that aims to make EdgeR DEG analysis as simple and automated as possible using featureCounts outputs. Default edgeR parameters include TMM normalization and both QLF and LRT tests. It uses on one hand a correspondance file with the following structure on each line: order,name,file_name,correspondance,group_1,group_2,group_3,group_4 Like for example: 1,A2-18-1,A2-18-1.bam,A_4E_18_2,A,4E,18,2 Please note that file_name should correspond to the column name of the featureCounts file and we do not need the actual bam file. Also, in order to automate as much as possible the analysis the design contrast is automatically generated assuming that: Group1=Species; Group2=Stade; Group3=Condition; Group4=Replicate TO DO: Describe how the desired contrasts can be obtained from the options. The other needed file is either a single featureCounts output file containing columns for all the samples, or individual featureCounts output files for each sample.

Script initially by David Armisen, later modified by Aleix Palahí. The original source can be found in: <https://gitlab.com/davidarmisen/edger-deg-analysis-using-featurecounts-output>

If you use this work, please cite this repository.

# TPM function
# michael's version
# https://support.bioconductor.org/p/91218/
##############

tpm <- function(x) { # From formula in https://www.biostars.org/p/322114/ . Same results as my tpm.DGEList function
  y<-as.data.frame(rpkm(x))
  return(t(t(y)*1e6/colSums(y)))
}

tpm.default <- function(counts,len,log=FALSE) {
  x <- counts/len
  y <- t(t(x)*1e6/colSums(x))
  if (log){
    y<-log2(y)
  }
  return(y)
}

tpm.DGEList <- function (y, gene.length = NULL, normalized.lib.sizes = TRUE, log = FALSE, prior.count = 2, ...){
    if (is.character(gene.length)) {
        gene.length <- y$genes[[gene.length[1]]]
        if (is.null(gene.length))
            stop("gene.length column not found")
    } else {
        if (is.null(gene.length))
            gene.length <- y$genes$Length
        if (is.null(gene.length))
            gene.length <- y$genes$length
        if (is.null(gene.length)) {
            j <- grep("length", tolower(names(y$genes)))
            if (length(j) == 1)
                gene.length <- y$genes[, j]
            else stop("Gene lengths not found")
        }
    }
  
    cnt = y$counts
    len = gene.length 
    
    norm.factors <- y$samples
    for (i in colnames(cnt)){
        cnt[,i]<-cnt[,i]*norm.factors[i,"norm.factors"]
    }
    
    tpm.default(counts=cnt,len=len,log=log)
}

# https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/3051/mean-of-a-sliding-window-in-r
# http://coleoguy.blogspot.com/2014/04/sliding-window-analysis.html
slideFunct <- function(data, window, step){
    total <- length(data)
    spots <- seq(from=1, to=(total-window), by=step)
    if (spots[length(spots)]<=total-window){spots<-c(spots,(spots[length(spots)]+step))} # Adapted to recover the last bits inside smaller window
    result <- vector(length = length(spots))
    for(i in 1:length(spots)){
      if ((spots[i]+window)>=total){window=(total-spots[i])} # Adapted to recover the last bits inside last smaller window 
      result[i] <- mean(data[spots[i]:(spots[i]+window-1)])
    }
    return(result)
  }
slideFunctDistance <- function(data1, window, step){
    total <- nrow(data1)
    spots <- seq(from=1, to=(total-window), by=step)
    if (spots[length(spots)]<=total-window){spots<-c(spots,(spots[length(spots)]+step))} # Adapted to recover the last bits inside smaller window
    result <- vector(length = length(spots))
    for(i in 1:length(spots)){
      if ((spots[i]+window)>=total){window=(total-spots[i])} # Adapted to recover the last bits inside last smaller window 
      if (window!=0){result[i] <- data1[(spots[i]+window-1)]$Mean-data1[spots[i]]$Mean}
      if (window==0){result[i] <- data1[spots[i]]$Mean}  # In case our group consists on a single gene
    }
    return(result)
  }

# Read files functions
######################
dag_load_files<-function(
  correspondance_file=NULL,
  functional_annotation_file=NULL,
  chromosome_size_file=NULL,
  subgenomes_file=NULL,
  gff3_file=NULL
){
  # Start empty variables to return them later
  correspondance<-NULL
  functional_annotation<-NULL
  chrom_size<-NULL
  subgenomes<-NULL
  gff_annotation<-NULL
  gene_coordinates<-NULL

  # Read correspondance's file
  if (length(correspondance_file)!=0){
    correspondance=fread(correspondance_file,header=TRUE,sep=",")
    # Format : order	name	file_name	correspondance	group_1	group_2	group_3	group_4
    
    #Define NEW samples names adapted for simplified analysis: Species_Stade_Condition_Replicate
    correspondance$new_name = c(paste0(correspondance$group_1,"_",correspondance$group_2,"_",correspondance$group_3,"_",correspondance$group_4))
  }  

  # Read functional annotation
  if (length(functional_annotation_file)!=0){
    functional_annotation=read.csv(file=functional_annotation_file,header=TRUE,sep ="\t")
    functional_annotation<-as.data.table(functional_annotation)
    functional_annotation$Simp.Gene.ID <-gsub("\\.[0-9]*$","",functional_annotation$Gene.ID,perl=TRUE)
  }
  
  
  # Chromosomes size 
  if (length(chromosome_size_file)!=0){
    chrom_size=read.csv(file=chromosome_size_file,header=TRUE,sep ="\t")
  }
  
  # Chromosomes subgenomes if any 
  if (length(subgenomes_file)!=0){
    subgenomes=read.csv(file=subgenomes_file,header=FALSE,sep ="\t")
    for(i in 1:nrow(subgenomes)){
      assign(paste0(subgenomes[i,]$V1),as.vector(strsplit(subgenomes[i,]$V2,","))[[1]])
    }
  }
    
  # Load annotations
  if (length(gff3_file)!=0){
    gff_annotation<-read.delim(gff3_file, header=F, comment.char="#")
    gff_annotation<-as.data.table(gff_annotation)
    colnames(gff_annotation)<-c("seqid","source","type","start","end","score","strand","phase","attributes")
  }
  
    
  
  # Gene coordinates
  if (length(gff3_file)!=0){
    x=fread(gff3_file,header=FALSE,sep="\t")
    colnames(x)<-c("Chromosome","Source","Type","Start","End","6","Strand","8","Gene")
    x$Gene=(gsub(".*ID=","",x$Gene, perl=TRUE))
    x$Gene=(gsub(";.*","",x$Gene, perl=TRUE))
    gene_coordinates<-x
    gene_coordinates$Mean=rowMeans(gene_coordinates[,c(4,5)])
  }
  
  
  return(list(correspondance=correspondance,
              functional_annotation=functional_annotation,
              chrom_size=chrom_size,
              subgenomes=subgenomes,
              gff_annotation=gff_annotation,
              gene_coordinates=gene_coordinates
  ))
}

# Read files and summarize mapped reads to RefSeq genes : Put counts into DGEList
dag_readfiles <- function(files, readsfolder=NULL, readsprefix=NULL, readssufix=NULL,correspondance=NULL,consolidateprojectreads=NULL,gene_coordinates=NULL,reduceprojectreads=NULL,columns_or_file_names="file") {
  for (l in 1:length(files)){
    i=files[l]

    j=""  
    for (fol in readsfolder){
      for (pre in readsprefix){
        for (suf in readssufix){
          t=paste0(fol,pre,i,suf)
          if (file.exists(t)){
            j=t
          }
          else (print(paste0("Error: files ",t," doesn't exists")))
        } 
      }      
    }

    y=fread(j,header=TRUE,sep="\t",na.strings=".",skip=1)
    colnames(y)[1:6]<-c("Geneid","Chr","Start","End","Strand","Length")

    ##########################################
    # Filter out here once for all ChrUn genes
    y<-y[!y$Chr %like% "chrUn",]
    ##########################################

    for (ll in 7:length(colnames(y))){
      lll<-colnames(y)[ll]
      colnames(y)[ll]<-"sample"
      if (l==1 & ll==7){
        counts<-y[,c("Geneid","sample")]
        genes<-y[,c("Geneid","Length")]
        colnames(y)[ll]<-lll
      } else {
        counts<-merge(counts,y[,c("Geneid","sample")], by="Geneid",all=TRUE);counts[is.na(counts)] <- 0
        if (y[,c("Geneid")] %in% genes[,c("Geneid")]){ # If we have new genes. i.e. reading samples from another a bam with only subgenome D and another from a bam with subgenome ABD
          genes<-merge(genes,y[!y$Geneid %in% genes$Geneid,c("Geneid","Length")], by=c("Geneid","Length"),all=TRUE)
        }
        colnames(y)[ll]<-lll
      }
      if (columns_or_file_names %in% "file"){
        i<-correspondance[correspondance$file_name %in% i , "correspondance"] # This allow to fix samples problems like i.e. Langdon 500T1 250T2
        names(counts)[names(counts) == 'sample'] <- as.character(i$correspondance) # I had to do this and use an intermediate 'sample' name because merge doesn't want to use a variable i directly. Need to check this in the future
      }
      else if (columns_or_file_names %in% "columns"){
        i<-correspondance$correspondance[correspondance$file_name %in% lll]
        names(counts)[names(counts) == 'sample'] <- as.character(i) # I had to do this and use an intermediate 'sample' name because merge doesn't want to use a variable i directly. Need to check this in the future
      }
    }
  }

  # Used it we have multiple copies of the same data. Developed to take into account original unsuccessful sequencing of brachy as well as the redone sequencing
  if (length(consolidateprojectreads)!=0){ 
    temp<-as.data.frame(counts)
    rownames(temp)<-temp[,"Geneid"]
    temp<-temp[,!colnames(temp) %in% "Geneid"]
    
    colnames(temp)<-gsub(consolidateprojectreads,"",colnames(temp),perl=TRUE)
    temp2<-unique(colnames(temp))
  
    temp<-t(rowsum(t(temp), group = colnames(temp), na.rm = T)) # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/35626945/row-wise-sum-of-values-grouped-by-columns-with-same-name
    temp<-as.data.frame(temp)
    temp[,"Geneid"]<-rownames(temp)
    temp<-as.data.table(temp)
    PROJECT_files<-temp2
    temp2<-c("Geneid",temp2)
    counts<-  temp[,..temp2]
  }
  
  # Changes samples names
  x<-colnames(counts[,2:ncol(counts)])
  y<-correspondance[correspondance %in% x,c("correspondance","new_name")]
  t<-y[match(x, y$correspondance),]$new_name
  colnames(counts)<-c("Geneid",t)
  t<-sort(t)
  t<-c("Geneid",t)
  counts<-counts[,..t]
  #
  projectreads<-dag_readsummary(counts=counts,lengths=genes,files=PROJECT_files,correspondance_files=correspondance)
  if (length(gene_coordinates)!=0){
    projectreads$genes<-unique(merge(projectreads$genes,gene_coordinates[Gene %in% projectreads$genes$Geneid,c("Chromosome","Gene")],by.x="Geneid",by.y="Gene"))
  }
  if (length(reduceprojectreads)!=0){
    projectreads <- projectreads[, colnames(projectreads[,colnames(projectreads) %like% reduceprojectreads]) , keep.lib.sizes=FALSE]
  }
  rownames(projectreads$genes)<-projectreads$genes$Geneid
 
  # Make sure order of genes is the same in projectreads$genes is the same as in projectreads$counts. Otherwise we can have problems later when filtering with keep
  projectreads$genes<-projectreads$genes[sort(projectreads$genes$Geneid),]
  projectreads$counts<-projectreads$counts[sort(projectreads$genes$Geneid),]
  
  return(projectreads)
}

# Read summarization. Summarize mapped reads to RefSeq genes. This will just take a few seconds. Note that the featureCounts function has built-in annotation for Refseq genes. featureCounts returns an R 'List' object, which includes raw read count for each gene in each library and also annotation information for genes such as gene identifiers and gene lengths. 
dag_readsummary <- function(counts,lengths,files,groups="",correspondance_files=NULL){
  Geneid<-counts$Geneid
  counts$Geneid<-NULL
  counts<-as.matrix(counts)
  rownames(counts)<-Geneid
  
  i<-NULL
  if (length(groups)==1){
    i<-gsub("_[0-9]*$","",colnames(counts),perl=TRUE);
  } else {i<-groups}
  groups=factor(i)
  t<-DGEList(counts = counts, genes=lengths, group=groups)

  tt<-correspondance_files[correspondance_files$new_name %in% colnames(counts),]
  
  # Add some information about samples i.e. species, stage, condition, replicate... 
  if (!is.null(correspondance_files$group_1)){t$group1<-data.frame(group=as.character(tt$group_1),row.names=tt$new_name)}
  if (!is.null(correspondance_files$group_2)){t$group2<-data.frame(group=as.character(tt$group_2),row.names=tt$new_name)}
  if (!is.null(correspondance_files$group_3)){t$group3<-data.frame(group=as.character(tt$group_3),row.names=tt$new_name)}
  if (!is.null(correspondance_files$group_4)){t$group4<-data.frame(group=as.character(tt$group_4),row.names=tt$new_name)}
      
  return(t)
}

# Filter genes by n method reads in m libraries and/or select the most highly expressed ones
# select data for the 'select' most highly expressed genes and decide if return the original or the transformed selection
dag_selectgenes <- function(data,gene.length=NULL,method="Raw",min=0,libraries=0,select=0,original=1,prior.count=2){
  check=0
  if(!is.null(names(data))){ # To avoid errors due to null values in next evaluation
    if(as.data.table(names(data)) %like% "counts"){ # Use DGEfile which allow also for calc.norm normaliztion in CPM, TPM and RPKM
      if (method=="Raw"){transfcounts <- data$counts}
      else if (method=="CPM"){transfcounts <- cpm(data,prior.count=prior.count)}
      else if (method=="TPM"){transfcounts <- tpm.DGEList(data,prior.count=prior.count)}
      else if (method=="RPKM"){transfcounts <- rpkm(data,prior.count=prior.count)}
      if (log==TRUE){transfcounts<-log2(transfcounts+1)}
    }
    else {print(paste("There is an error in input data type"))}
  }
  else {
    if (method=="Raw"){transfcounts <- data}
    else if (method=="CPM"){transfcounts <- cpm(data,prior.count=prior.count)}
    else if (method=="TPM"){transfcounts <- tpm.default(data,gene.length=gene.length,prior.count=prior.count)}
    else if (method=="RPKM"){transfcounts <- rpkm(data,gene.length=gene.length,prior.count=prior.count)}
    if (log==TRUE){transfcounts<-log2(transfcounts+1)}
  }

  # Filter those genes which had >'min' 'method' reads in at least 'libraries' libraries.
  transfcounts <- transfcounts[(rowSums(transfcounts >= min) >= libraries),]
  counts<-transfcounts

  datas<-data
  
  if (original==0){ #  Modify to return the calculated values
    datas <- counts  # If I already calculated CPM, TPM, RPKM I no longer need DGElist object
  }

  if (select!=0){resultscounts <- datas[order(rowMeans(counts), decreasing=TRUE)[1:select],]}
  else {resultscounts <- datas[rownames(counts),]}

  return(resultscounts)
}

# To simplify groups when we have extracted a subset from our main DEGList data object
dag_simplify_groups<-function(data){ # It also reorder columns
    keep<-colnames(data$counts)
    data$group1$sample<-rownames(data$group1);data$group1<-data$group1[rownames(data$group1) %in% keep,];rownames(data$group1)<-data$group1$sample
    data$group2$sample<-rownames(data$group2);data$group2<-data$group2[rownames(data$group2) %in% keep,];rownames(data$group2)<-data$group2$sample
    data$group3$sample<-rownames(data$group3);data$group3<-data$group3[rownames(data$group3) %in% keep,];rownames(data$group3)<-data$group3$sample
    data$group4$sample<-rownames(data$group4);data$group4<-data$group4[rownames(data$group4) %in% keep,];rownames(data$group4)<-data$group4$sample
    
    return(data)
}

dag_folders_name<-function(prefix,prefix2,subgenome="none",filtermin,filterminlib,filter_low,padjusted){
  name=paste0(prefix)

  folder=paste0("outputs_",filtermin,"_",filterminlib,"_",filter_low,"_",prefix2,"_",padjusted,"/")
  folderPCA<-paste0(folder,"PCA/")
  folderData<-paste0(folder,"data/")
  folderUpset<-paste0(folder,"Upset-Venn/")
  folderedgeR<-paste0(folder,"edgeR/")
  folderDensities<-paste0(folder,"Densities/")
  folderGO<-paste0(folder,"GO/")
  folderAdditivity<-paste0(folder,"Additivity/")
  folderDynamic<-paste0(folder,"Dynamic/")
    
  dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderPCA, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderData, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderUpset, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderedgeR, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderDensities, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderGO, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderAdditivity, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(folderDynamic, showWarnings = FALSE)
  
  return(list(name=name,
              folder=folder,
              folderPCA=folderPCA,
              folderData=folderData,
              folderUpset=folderUpset,
              folderedgeR=folderedgeR,
              folderDensities=folderDensities,
              folderGO=folderGO,
              folderAdditivity=folderAdditivity,
              folderDynamic=folderDynamic
  ))
}
